short: How far a soldier believes in you as her commander. It decides whether she obeys, refuses or walks away.
long: Trust runs from 0 to 100. It rises when you keep promises, protect her and decide in ways she respects; it falls when you lie, coerce her or leave people behind. When it drops, her [[loyalty_band|loyalty]] wavers. The Leash can force an order, but it costs Trust.

short: Personal warmth toward you, from cold to devoted. Unlike Trust it is about the person, not the rank.
long: Affinity runs from -100 to 100. It grows through kindness, shared time and being on her side, and sinks through insults, betrayals and coercion. Together with the other axes it decides which [[relationship_state|relationship state]] she can reach.

short: Romantic or physical interest, 0 to 100. It only grows while romance is switched on and she has reason to like you.
long: Attraction opens the romantic relationship states, but never forces them: a state also needs an event or a proposal. Switch romance off in the [[setting:romance|romance setting]] and it stays out of every reading and scene.

short: Strain on a soldier, 0 to 100. It sharpens her defects and, at the top, breaks her.
long: Fights, danger, refused orders and Leash use raise it; rest, calm company and the medbay lower it. It moves her through four bands: calm, strained, breaking and breakdown. Stress is not a relationship axis, but it changes how every defect plays.

short: From 50 Stress: the downsides of her defects bite harder and passives tied to Stress start to fire.
From 80 Stress: each turn she may lose control and act on her defect's breakdown instead of your orders.
At 100 Stress she breaks down: her defect's breakdown plays out until the expedition ends and she is released.
Out of the fight at 0 HP. Some skills can revive her; afterwards she is injured. A downed grunt may die, a named unit never does in combat.
Steady, wavering or breaking: how close she is to refusing orders or leaving.
long: It follows Trust with a delay, so it does not flicker: she turns wavering below 25 and breaking below 10, and recovers only at 35 and 20. Wavering units sometimes refuse orders; breaking ones may desert, and from the worst relationship states, mutiny.

short: Where your bond with a soldier stands: Stranger, Friend, Rival, Resentful and more. A state is entered through events, not numbers alone.
long: States unlock scenes, night visits, combat synergies and defect arcs, and they change how a soldier obeys and speaks. Axes and flags set the stage; an event or a proposal turns the page.

short: Six axes, from -3 to +3, that describe what a soldier cares about. They decide how she reacts to your decisions.
Results over principles. High: accepts ugly means for good ends. Low: refuses to cross lines.
Wants to choose for herself. High: bristles at orders and the Leash. Low: at ease being told what to do.
Loyalty to the squad. High: no one is left behind. Low: the mission comes first.
Compassion for the weak and the beaten. High: hates needless harm. Low: ruthless.
Faith in the corporation and its rules. High: follows the chain of command. Low: distrusts every contract.
Willingness to pay a price for others. High: gives herself first. Low: protects her own skin.
Your four social ranks, 1 to 5. They gate options and decide social rolls.
Making people follow. Used to talk a deserter down, press an order and hold a room.
Reading people and situations. Used to spot lies and hidden motives.
Understanding and comforting. Used to calm, reach and persuade through care.
Scheming and bargaining. Used for bluffs and clever deals; it also pays on contract work.
Money for upgrades, recruits, crafting and requisitions. Earned from contract work and missions.
Food, medicine and ammunition. Everyone eats every day; a shortage costs stress and goodwill.
Programmable polymer: the material for crafting and upgrading gear. Scarce, and needed for defect arcs.
The supplies the base eats each day: one per living soldier, reserve included, and one for you. A mess hall lowers it.
long: A day without enough supplies costs stress and Affinity across the squad, and after three days in a row it costs Trust too. Requisition more supplies with credits, or lower the bill with the mess hall.

short: Time comes in slots: morning, afternoon, evening and, only when something happens, night. Activities, talks and expeditions spend them.
You are hurt: training and work are blocked until you recover. Lovers and dependents may come to see you.
Command Points, your combat resource. Spend them on orders and ultimates; you gain one each round, up to five.
A corporate override you can request: Compel, Suppress or Terminate. Authorizations refill weekly, and every use costs relations.
long: Each request goes through an oversight form. Every use is logged, the squad notices, and soldiers who value their autonomy hate it. A soldier you leash may not forgive you.

short: Forces one order: in a scene her next reply complies, in combat it cancels a refusal. Costs Trust and Affinity and adds stress.
long: It spends one authorization. The target loses Trust and Affinity and gains stress; witnesses react according to their values, and repeated use can turn her resentful.

short: Stops a desertion or an attack in progress. Costs a lot of Trust and unsettles the whole squad.
Permanent deactivation. Needs a cause and an oversight approval, and the squad will not forget it.
A mandatory malfunction every soldier carries: an upside, a downside and a breakdown. It changes how she plays, not how strong she is.
A personal storyline about a defect: Cure, Manage or Embrace. It opens with trust, medbay level and time.
Removes the defect, upside included. She may feel like a stranger to herself.
Softens the downside and keeps the upside, but needs regular upkeep at the medbay.
Amplifies both upside and downside, and turns the breakdown into something the squad can use, or fear.
What her defect does at 100 Stress: she stops following orders and acts on the malfunction until released.
Hit points. At zero she is downed. Grows with level and gear.
long: Role base, plus growth per level, plus gear and percentage bonuses; each injury cuts it by a tenth, up to three injuries. Defects and statuses can change it for a fight.

short: Attack. It scales most of the damage she deals.
long: Damage is ATK times the skill multiplier, softened by the target's DEF. Weapons, affixes and some defects raise it, and effects that change damage dealt multiply the result.

short: Defense. It soaks part of every hit she takes.
long: Incoming damage is reduced by 100 divided by 100 plus DEF. Armor and some effects raise it; effects that change damage taken apply on top.

short: Speed. It decides who acts first each round.
long: Higher SPD acts earlier. Heavy armor lowers it by up to three; weapons can add or take away a point or two.

short: Critical chance, in percent. A critical hit deals one and a half times the damage.
Fights give experience; each level adds stats and one skill point. Your clearance caps how high she can go.
One per level. Spend them in her skill tree on actives, passives and upgrades. A respec costs plyx and credits.
The skills she brings into a fight: four actives, plus her signature and ultimate. Change them on her sheet between fights.
Standard, refined, prototype, corporate or anomalous. Higher rarity means stronger stats and more affix slots; anomalous gear carries a drawback.
Craft, upgrade, reroll and dismantle gear. Each workshop activity opens a session with a few operations.
The four soldiers who go on expeditions. The rest wait in reserve; your barracks decide how many beds you have.
A generated soldier: ASCII portrait, Trust only, and mortal. Cheap to recruit, and a grunt who drops to zero HP can die.
A corporate access tier that raises the level cap. Story beats and base upgrades grant it: ten, twenty, thirty, then forty.
An unscouted spot on the expedition map. What it is shows only when you are near it or step in.
One choice in a decision. It tells you what it asks of you, never what it will change.
A small decision with modest stakes, often met on an expedition.
A weighty decision that can shift relations, resources or the world.
A rare decision the story will remember.
How hard the mission's fights are, 1 to 5. Higher danger means tougher enemies and better loot.
The class of payout for finishing the mission: credits, plyx, loot and standing with the corporation all grow with the tier.
Days left to start the mission. When they run out the offer lapses, and some missions cost you when they do.
Missions on offer. Command and story missions stay posted; side jobs and rumor leads can be dismissed. Comms upgrades make the board bigger.
A mission run on a node map: you pick four soldiers, their rows and the supplies to carry, then walk the map. It spends the morning and the afternoon.
Overheard gossip from the base. Some rumors lead to a mission or a place worth scouting; the rest is atmosphere.
The connection profile of the mechanic model: it reads conversations and writes structured data.
How much the mechanic model may think before it answers. Minimal is cheapest; provider default leaves it alone.
With no mechanic profile set, use the main model for mechanic calls.
The smallest token limit sent on a mechanic call, so models that think have room to finish.
Expected output tokens per call type. Lower is cheaper; too low cuts answers short and forces a retry.
The most tokens the Alius context block may add to each main-model prompt.
The phosphor color of the Alius screen: amber, green or white.
Faint CRT scanlines over the screen.
A slight CRT flicker. Turn it off if it strains your eyes.
Shows model calls, prompts, content errors and the raw campaign state in the SYS tab.
Keeps mechanics view-only. Turn it off to edit the campaign state in the debug panel.
Allows Desire and Bond defects in imports and lists. A running campaign keeps the value it started with.
Shows exact numbers for relationships and stress instead of bands.
How a character's expression is chosen: by SillyTavern's own Expressions, or by the mechanic model.
A short generated vignette after an activity done with a companion (main model, one call each).
A generated name and one-line bio for newly recruited grunts.
When the mechanic model reads a conversation: after every exchange, every few exchanges, or only when the scene ends.
How many exchanges to wait between readings when the model reads every few exchanges.
Readings the model is less sure of than this are dropped.
After this many exchanges the scene header says time is passing.
How fast dialogue types out, in characters per second. Zero shows it at once.
Switches romantic states, Attraction and proposals on or off.
Tells the main model whether explicit scenes are allowed. What it writes still depends on your model and preset.
How often soldiers make romantic moves on their own: low, medium or high.
Lets soldiers start private messages with you on their own.
Condenses old chronicle lines with the mechanic model instead of just joining them.
Lets you rewind a lost combat and try again. The story does not remember rewinds.
Generated names for affixed enemies. Cached, and never holds up a fight.
Lets the mechanic model plan missions, rumors and story beats. Off: the engine's own fallback plans the world.
The minimum number of days between two story-beat proposals.
A narrative after-action recap written by the main model. The plain report always exists.
Lets the mechanic model write decisions. Off: the authored options of the template are shown.
Turns the analysis tool on or off: hover, press ? or long-press anything to read what it does.
How long the ANALYZING line plays: full (longer the first time), short, or off.
How long to hover before the analysis panel opens, in milliseconds.
Combat difficulty of this campaign: story, normal or hard. It scales enemy health, attack and defense.
How many days units take to stop judging the commander by his looks. The first meeting counts most.
